correctness.rationale: Pass for the complete repaired RESULT.md. The frozen inducing formula is not valid as stated for every measure with positive marker mass: a mixture of a renewal measure and the marker-free measure induces only the renewal component. The repair applies it on each ergodic component and uses affinity, and justifies finite marginal entropy and iid equality. Also the frozen derivative equivalent at t=0 had a zero comparison term; the repair uses a scaled limit there. Independently, the rotation partition gives the heavy-factor count by counting endpoints in [1−{nα},1); a mesh argument gives uniform discrepancy for this moving interval. Equidistribution of {nα} makes the two centered counts, with limiting weights 1−q and q, contribute the triangular density 1−|y| on [−1,1]. Its Laplace transform is (2sinh(t/2)/t)², which stays positive at every real t. Abel summation of the weighted Cesàro averages gives the n and n² constants and the fixed-δ color derivative limit, including t=0. The return mean is asymptotic to 2/δ and the centered count mean tends to I'/I, proving both occupation laws. The exact x=4sinh²(P/2) identity and evenness of the color factor verify the zero-field and slope formulas. The theorem's parameters and conclusions are unchanged; the finite verify.py was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: This is a singular thermodynamic regime with a genuine identification problem: even the entire marker-only curve cannot separate slopes. The evaluated nonlinear color amplitude separates them and predicts both leading marker density and the associated color redistribution. The distinction between weighting distinct factors and sampling them by invariant occurrence frequencies is essential; the precise amplitude is not a renaming of word complexity.
